intro: Work out how fast something changes from a table of measurements, and compare samples fairly with percent change.
howItWorksTitle: The formulas, and how answers are checked
howItWorks:
rate = Δy / Δt = (y₂ − y₁) / (t₂ − t₁)

percent change = (final − initial) / initial × 100

  • A rate always has a unit made of two units: the amount per unit of time (for example mL/min).
  • Percent change compares each sample with its own starting value. A loss gives a negative percent change: keep the sign.
  • An answer counts when it is within one unit of the last decimal place asked for, or within 1%.
